concept.name: Zigzag indicator
concept.definition: A price filter rather than a true indicator: it draws straight legs between swing points, ignoring all moves smaller than a set percentage (traditionally 5%), to reveal the significant highs and lows through the noise.
concept.intuition: It answers 'what would this chart look like if every wiggle under x% were deleted?' - exposing the skeleton of swings for trend, pattern, and Elliott Wave analysis.
concept.mechanics: Track price from the last confirmed pivot; extend the current leg while price moves favorably, and confirm a new pivot only after a reversal of at least the threshold percentage. On bar/candle charts the filter uses the high-low range, on line charts the closes.
concept.formula: A pivot is confirmed when |P_t - P_pivot| / P_pivot >= threshold (e.g., 5%); legs connect successive confirmed pivots.
concept.failure_modes: The last leg is provisional and repaints until the threshold is met - ZigZag is hindsight by design, and StockCharts states explicitly that it has no predictive power.
concept.misconceptions: The clean historical legs are not tradeable signals; the current leg can disappear entirely if the reversal threshold is never reached.
concept.example: From a 100 low, price rises to 112 (+12%): the leg extends to 112; only a decline to 100.8 (-10% with a 10% setting) confirms a new down leg.
